key_insight: An intermediate loading of 4 wt.% nominal Pd optimized spray-coated MoS2 films, delivering 88.1% methylene blue degradation in 40 minutes under LED irradiation without changing the optical gap.
engineering_relevance: Pd loading offers a route to improve visible-light photocatalytic coatings through crystalline ordering and potentially charge separation rather than band-gap tuning.
method: Sol–gel spray-coated quartz with undoped and 2, 4, or 6 wt.% nominal Pd-doped MoS2; sulfurized at 800 °C.
Characterized structure, vibrations, and optical properties using XRD, Raman, FTIR, and optical spectroscopy.
Evaluated methylene blue degradation under a 20 W LED against photolysis.
evidence_signal: At 4% Pd, the coherent domain size reached 62.3 nm and the apparent degradation rate constant was 0.0483 min⁻¹, 1.29× the undoped value; degradation fell to 57.8% at 6% Pd.
watch_item: Pd-mediated charge separation is a proposed explanation, not an independently verified mechanism.
paper_title: Pd-doped MoS2 thin films grown by sol–gel spray coating: structural, vibrational and optical modifications and their impact on photocatalytic degradation of methylene blue under LED irradiation
